value.rationale: One random material sample per cell is a natural low-cost approximation for unresolved heterogeneous interfaces. The complete exact distribution separates its generically first-order random flux error from second-order bias; full phase-limit failure versus triangular Cesaro mixture supplies a genuinely structural uncertainty benchmark, and the exact Galerkin comparison identifies a distinct first-order deterministic interface flux bias. These facts require precise invariants and are not asserted to improve general discretization error or runtime.
